title: Implement steady-state solver
action: Write a Python module that implements the numerical steady-state solver described in the Mathematical model section. The module must provide a function `compute_u_stat(eta, Q, a, b, gamma)` that solves the normalized ODE (1) during the closed-switch period, computes the voltage change during the open period via (3), and finds u_stat by numerically solving equation (4) (e.g., using bisection or scipy.optimize). Use the fixed normalization α=1, C_p=1, x̂_p=1. The function returns u_stat as a float.
description: The model will be used in the subsequent scored step to produce the required artifacts.

title: Compute voltage table, optimal switching, and equivalence
action: Using the implemented solver, generate a single JSON file `/app/outputs/analytical_results.json` containing three parts: (I) voltage_table: compute u_stat for each of the specified parameter tuples (η, Q, a, b, γ) listed in the instruction, (II) optimal_law: perform a grid search over a∈[-0.5,0.5], b∈[0.3,0.7] with step ≤0.01 for η=0.5, Q=10, γ=0 to find a_opt, b_opt and peak_voltage, (III) equivalence: compute α* from u_stat at γ=0 and γ=0.2 with optimal switching and verify α*≈α+Cpγ.
description: This scored artifact contains the voltage table (including gamma field), the optimal switching law, and the force factor equivalence check. The verifier will recompute the values using its own implementation of the same model and compare them within hidden tolerances.
output_schema: {"voltage_table": [{"eta": float, "Q": float, "a": float, "b": float, "gamma": float, "u_stat": float}], "optimal_law": {"a_opt": float, "b_opt": float, "peak_voltage": float}, "equivalence": {"gamma": float, "alpha_eff": float, "alpha_plus": float, "match": bool}}
